- Strong demand for AI, cloud, cybersecurity and digital engineering talent may raise talent acquisition costs and impact delivery capability and project execution if the Company cannot attract, retain and develop specialized professionals.
- The business is described as capital-intensive, creating pressure on working capital; growth may be hampered if adequate funding is not available.
- Failure to continuously invest in upskilling, innovation and service transformation to keep pace with technological change may impact competitiveness.
- Increasing cyber threats, evolving data protection regulations and heightened customer expectations on information security could cause operational, financial and reputational harm if not effectively managed.
- Economic slowdowns, inflationary pressures, geopolitical developments, and changes in trade policy may influence client spending patterns and technology investment decisions.
- Delays in customer decision-making, reductions in discretionary technology spending, or shifts in client priorities may impact revenue growth and project pipelines.
- Domestic and international regulatory frameworks covering data privacy, labor, tax and technology may increase compliance obligations and operating costs.
